 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. You
  will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-35 AND 19-36 SETTING THE RATE
  AND AMOUNT NECESSARY FOR THE 2019-20 FISCAL YEAR RETIREMENT
  TAX LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy authorized
  by the voters in 1948. The special property tax levy approved by the voters
  requires the City Council to annually establish a tax rate sufficient to meet the
  City’s obligations to the state employees’ retirement system. Each year, the City
  approves a tax rate necessary to generate revenues not to exceed the amount
  needed to meet the retirement obligations. No change in the tax rate is
  recommended for the 2019-20 fiscal year and the City Council is asked to
  confirm the current rate and fix the amount of property taxes to be generated
  by adopting two Resolutions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-35, setting the
  tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution 19-36, fixing
  the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City’s employees’
  retirement cost for fiscal year 2019-20.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2019  3
   E. GREAT STREETS PROGRAM (PROJECT #1-08-35) CHANGE PURCHASE
  ORDER REQUEST (CONTRACT NO. 18-05)

  In October 2018, City Council awarded a construction contract to Palp, Inc. DBA
  Excel Paving Company for the Great Streets Program. The project consisted of
  rehabilitation of pavement on various street segments around the City
  including Mission Drive and San Marino Avenue. Additional work was added to
  the original project scope and the project was completed in May 2019. The final
  construction cost is $1,716,059.34, which is $125,567.14 (7.9%) over the
  approved construction budget. Staff is requesting City Council approve a
  change purchase order request in the amount of $125,567.14 and use available
  Measure “M” funding within the Great Streets Program budget.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends the City Council:
  1. Approve the use of $125,567. 14 of Great Streets Program project funding
  for the cost overrun of the Great Streets Program.
  2. Authorize staff to approve a Change Purchase Order Request for Purchase
  Order number 8011 in the amount of $125,567.14

  F. CONTRACT WITH CINTAS CORPORATION FOR UNIFORM SERVICE FOR
  THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  The Public Works Department requires all field staff to wear a City issued
  uniform. This includes all Field Operations, Parks Maintenance, Facilities, and
  Fleet personnel. In the past, the City purchased uniforms for the Field
  Operations, Parks Maintenance and Facilities Maintenance staff every two years,
  and the Fleet Division is currently under contract with Cintas Corporation for
  their uniform service. The field staff which is issued City purchased uniforms are
  required to wash, maintain, and repair their own uniforms. Each employee is
  issued 10 uniforms. The City also purchases additional uniforms on an as
  needed basis. The Fleet Division uniform service will fall under the new
  agreement. The annual cost of service will not exceed $16,500.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the 3-year Contract with Cintas
  Uniform Service and approve a Purchase Order in the amount not to exceed
  $16,500 per year from accounts1221-800-02-43-000 ($14,500) and 137-800-
  01-43-000 ($2000).

  G. BANNER REQUEST- ALHAMBRA EDUCATIONAL FOUNDATION

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2019  4
   The City has received a banner request from the Alhambra Education
  Foundation (AEF). The AEF will be hosting a concert on Saturday, October 12,
  2019 to serve the surrounding cities as well as the San Gabriel community. This
  event will take place on 2nd Street in Alhambra located between Main Street
  and Commonwealth Avenue, Alhambra CA. Staff is requesting that the City
  Council approve the request to hang a street banner for the Alhambra
  Educational Foundation Magic in the Music at Las Tunas Drive and San Marino
  Avenue from September 16, 2019 to October 14, 2019.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council grant the request, subject to
  compliance with Section 153.334 (A) of the Municipal Code and the street
  banner conditions as listed on page 2 of the street banner application form.

  H. RESOLUTION NO. 19-37 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE OF
  BRIDGE STREET, FROM SYCAMORE DRIVE TO THE NORTH END OF BRIDGE
  STREET ON SEPTEMBER 1, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request form Ray Abeyta for a
  temporary street closure for a neighborhood block party on Sunday, September
  1, 2019 from 3:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. of Bridge Street, from Sycamore Drive to
  the north end of Bridge Street. The street closure will enable the community
  members to congregate safely in a centralized location. Resolution No. 19-37
  (attached) details the location, date and times for the closure, as well as the
  conditions that must be followed by the applicant. The Public Works
  Department (Engineering and Field Operations), Fire Department and Police
  Department have reviewed and approved the request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-37 authorizing
  closure of Bridge Street, from Sycamore Drive to the north end of Bridge Street
  from 3:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. on Sunday, September 1, 2019.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PUBLIC HEARING – ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION NO. 19-31 TO UPDATE
  THE CITY’S CITYWIDE (MASTER) FEE SCHEDULE

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2019  5
   This item is continued from the July 16, 2019 Regular City Council Meeting. Staff
  requests that the Public Hearing be closed. The item will be rescheduled to be
  heard at a later time.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CITY-WIDE SPEED HUMP POLICY CONSIDERATION

  On January 15, 2019, Council directed staff to prepare a city-wide speed hump
  policy for Council consideration. During the July 2, 2019, City Council Meeting,
  the City Council directed staff to make several changes in the policy before
  returning to them for consideration. The changes include revising the fee
  schedule, developing a notification requirement, increasing the upper limit of
  the traffic (ADT) requirement, and consideration of the expected life cycle of
  the speed hump in the policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff requests that the City Council consider for approval the attached Speed
  Hump Policy For Residential Streets and provide direction to staff regarding the
  request for speed humps from the residents of Country Club Drive.

  B. CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST FROM THE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA GAS
  COMPANY TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO SUPPORT BALANCED ENERGY
  SOLUTIONS AND LOCAL CONTROL OF ENERGY SOLUTIONS

  In an attempt to reduce greenhouse gasses and global warming, the State of
  California is considering various mandates that are intended to make the State
  “greener”. The Southern California Gas Company has requested that the City of
  San Gabriel consider adopting a resolution that would demonstrate the City’s
  desire to achieve green standards using an approach that includes balanced
  energy choices and local control.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and consider adoption of the
  attached resolution.
